reasoning_traces.think:
The SportR benchmark introduces a structured multimodal reasoning framework grounded in expert-annotated chain-of-thought (CoT) protocols. It defines a progression from perception to conceptual understanding, enabling LLMs to reason about sports rules rather than merely recognize patterns. The core operators—Sports Image Reasoning, Progressive QA Hierarchy, and GRPO Training Recipe—are mathematically unified through a layered approach: visual input maps to structured CoT via macro-to-micro reasoning, which is then evaluated via progressive QA tasks. The GRPO training recipe ensures stable policy updates by combining clipped surrogates, advantage normalization, and KL penalties. This structure supports both rule-based reasoning and visual grounding, forming a dual logic of perception and cognition. Failure modes include CoT misalignment, policy drift under KL constraints, and insufficient grounding in complex video sequences. The framework's strength lies in its ability to decouple high-level reasoning from low-level perception, enabling modular extension and evaluation.
